artworks.title: The Sleep of Erigone
artworks.description: Lithograph in the Musée Carnavalet after Girodet's erotic-idyllic Erigone: Icarius' daughter asleep among vines — the Attic girl whom Dionysus loved before her father's murder and her own hanging grief.

artworks.title: Erigone Ensnared by Dionysus
artworks.description: Wellcome Collection print: Erigone reaches for grapes as Dionysus ensnares her in the vine — the seduction that precedes Icarius' gift of wine to the shepherds and the daughter's later suicide.

artworks.title: Erigone with Grapes (after Guido Reni)
artworks.description: Metropolitan Museum print after Reni: Erigone leans over a platter of grapes — the Attic heroine reduced to Bacchic beauty, still named for Icarius' daughter whose dog Maera found the unburied body.

popCulture.title: Erigone
popCulture.description: Daughter of Icarius of Attica; after finding her murdered father she hanged herself — catasterized with Maera, and remembered in the Attic Aiora festival.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid and the mythographers keep Erigone's grief in the Dionysus–Icarius cycle — wine, murder, and a daughter's rope among the Attic hills.
